source_text: Vide quam diversa sit naturae ratio et voluntatis. Non negavit Iesus, carnem eorum pertinere ad semen Abrahae, sed inculcat eis, quod ad diabolum patrem voluntatis iniquitate migraverint; qui ideo genitor eorum dicitur, quod criminum arguitur eruditor. Responderunt, inquit, et dixerunt ei Iudaei: Pater noster Abraham est. Dicit eis Iesus: Si filii Abrahae essetis, opera Abrahae faceretis; nunc autem quaeritis me interficere, hominem qui veritatem locutus sum vobis, quam audivi a Deo; hoc Abraham non fecit, vos autem facitis opera patris vestri [n209] . Aspicisne quas faciat verborum divisiones Sapientia? Negat eos Abrahae filios esse, quos supra dixerat esse filios Abrahae; sed quoniam diversus est de natura ac voluntate tractatus, ostendit alterum esse prosatorem carnis innocuae, alterum seductorem miserae voluntatis.
pass_a_gloss: See how diverse is the account of nature and of will. Jesus did not deny that their flesh pertains to the seed of Abraham, but he stamps in on them, that by iniquity of will they have migrated to the devil as father; who is therefore said their begetter, because he is argued the teacher of crimes. They answered, he says, and said to him, the Jews: Our father is Abraham. Jesus says to them: If you were sons of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham; but now you seek to kill me, a human who has spoken the truth to you, which I heard from God; this Abraham did not do, but you do the works of your father. Do you look at what divisions of words Wisdom makes? He denies them to be sons of Abraham, whom above he had said to be sons of Abraham; but since the treatise about nature and about will is diverse, he shows that one is the progenitor of harmless flesh, the other the seducer of a wretched will.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: See how different the accounts of nature and will are. Jesus did not deny that their flesh belonged to Abraham's offspring. But he presses upon them that through an unjust will they had moved to the devil as their father, who is called their begetter because he is shown to be their teacher in crimes. “The Jews answered and said to him, ‘Abraham is our father.’ Jesus said to them, ‘If you were Abraham's children, you would do Abraham's works. But now you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth I heard from God. Abraham did not do this; you do the works of your father’” (John 8:39–41). Do you see the distinctions Wisdom makes in its language? He denies that they are Abraham's children after saying above that they were Abraham's children. But because nature and will require different treatment, he shows that the ancestor of their innocent flesh is one person, and the deceiver of their wretched will another.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
